title: Architect geometric plan, plan/0 (FROZEN 2026-10-12; docs/CONTRACT.md 6c slice P0)
description: The geometric layer of a composed settlement plan (steward-mc docs/COMPOSITION.md §3; architect-mc docs/COMPOSITION-ANSWERS.md, its Revisions win). Claude writes it through Steward's plan writer; Regions.checkPlan answers each part. It holds no world coordinates: places are locators over features of the survey and named anchors, with an optional quantised relative sketch. Architect owns this schema, its compiler and the capability catalogue. Steward's life layer (story, stages, schedule, relations, secrets) is out of scope and points at parts through partRef and each part's ext. The file stays inside the keyword subset of kit/lib/specschema.mjs ($ref, oneOf, anyOf, type, enum, const, pattern, minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, minItems, maxItems, items, required, properties, additionalProperties: false); what that subset can't say is in x-rules, x-dispatch and x-defaults, which the plan validator (kit, P0) applies after the schema. Members may be added within plan/0 (additive, optional); any change to an existing member's meaning is a new schemaVersion. FROZEN 2026-10-12, after Steward's 59-ask fixtures round. From now on a change within plan/0 is additive only: a new optional member, a new reserved kind or block id, a new catalogue entry. Anything else (removing or renaming a member, narrowing a value, changing a meaning, making an optional member required) needs plan/1.
x-rules: R1 ids: every part id (zones, connectors, forms, rules) is unique across the whole plan, not per family

R2 references: every part id named anywhere (locator targets, endpoints, relief.around, dependencies, feature {part}) names a part of this plan; an unknown id makes the referring part malformed (reason UNKNOWN_REF)

R3 dependencies: the graph of explicit dependencies plus implicit ones (a part depends on every part its where, endpoints or around name) is acyclic; a cycle makes every part on it malformed (reason CYCLE)

R4 dispatch: each family's items are checked first against the loose base ($defs/partBase); then by x-dispatch on kind: a kind whose catalogue entry is supported is checked strictly against its $defs entry, and an error there makes the part malformed; a reserved, retired or unknown kind is checked only against $defs/extension and answers unsupported {block: <block id>}, never malformed (an envelope over its bounds is malformed)

R4a kinds and one-of members: a connector, form or rule has a kind; a zone without one is kind standard. A near locator names exactly one of anchor or feature; a sketch with frame anchor names its anchor; along with side toward_anchor or away_from_anchor names its anchor

R5 block ids: <family>.<kind> for parts (zone.standard, connector.wall, form.relief, rule.palette); program.<name> for a zone's program; locator.<form>, feature.<selector>, endpoint.<form> and sketch.<form> for the place vocabulary. A namespaced kind keeps its namespace: connector.steward:moat. An unsupported answer names the exact block id

R6 extension bounds: one extension part is at most 4096 characters as canonical JSON and nests at most 6 deep; at most 32 extension parts and 32768 characters of extension JSON per plan; over a bound the part is malformed (reason EXTENSION_BOUND)

R7 ext: a part's or the plan's ext has namespace:name keys (at most 200 characters each) and is at most 4096 characters as compact JSON; keys under architect_mc: are Architect's and a caller's value is dropped (as 6c X C19). Architect never reads a caller's ext; it is echoed in the part's answer and kept in the artifact
R8 ranges: an intRange [a, b] has a <= b; a sketch in unit q64 has coordinates 0..64, in unit block -512..512; a polygon sketch has at least 3 points
R9 one plan is at most 65536 characters as canonical JSON, and at most 128 parts in all

R10 numbers: every coordinate, distance and size is an integer in blocks (cells) unless its definition says otherwise; numbers that are not integers (grades, ratios) are quantised by the compiler to 1/64
R11 required parts: a part with required true whose answer is unsupported or refused blocks approval (COMPOSITION §2.5); a required rule that can't be verified blocks readiness
R12 notes and labels are free text: kept, shown, never treated as a verified requirement

R13 provisional parts: a part is provisional when a lot has no library entry or its style (own or inherited from the zone or plan) is {pending}. Its cost and palette are a range; the approval artifact records each provisional part's cost range and fit box; the approval is kept while the fit stays inside the lot box and the cost inside the range, and the caller re-approves past the top of the range (rebinding when the bible exists)

R4b layout: program.lots.layout is one of street, ring, spiral, grid or organic (supported; FL) or elevated (reserved until 7b). A reserved layout is checked like any supported lots program and the part answers unsupported {block: layout.<name>}, never malformed. A layout is written only there: not as a connector kind (connector.ring_street, connector.grid) nor as a rule kind (rule.ring_layout, rule.layout_ring)

R4c aliases: zone kind district is a reserved alias of the program form {districts}: the part answers unsupported {block: program.districts} (never zone.district) until D1, so one idea has one block id

R2a lots as places (P0, additive): where a part names a place (a locator target, a near feature, an endpoint) a lot id of a zone of this plan is accepted for a part id: it names that lot (an endpoint: its entrance), through its zone, which is then an implicit dependency (R3). A zone's port is one of its lots or bell, start or end (its street's two ends). Lot ids are unique across the plan (one region's lots)

R14 anchors: names are caller-supplied positions (PlanRequest.anchors) or the built-in claim_* ones; P0 never interprets a name. Steward passes stone, player, street_w, street_e, district_<id> and stockpile; an unknown anchor name used by a part is malformed (UNKNOWN_REF)

R15 walls (K1): a connector.wall has exactly one path form: from and to (with via[]: wall.line), where.around (wall.around), where.inside (wall.edge) or where.along (wall.along, reserved until K2); none or two is malformed

R16 gates (K1): a connector.gate's crossing names a street, road, path, rope_bridge or auto connector of this plan (UNKNOWN_REF otherwise); its wall names a wall of this plan; a gate written from/to (the envelope shape) is read as at: from, to noted as the side it faces

R17 doors (K1): door: door is a wooden double door, so the opening is 2 wide (1 on a 1-wide path); fence_gate is player-only (a crossing used by a villager edge refuses MOVER); params is read leniently and never makes a K1 part malformed: a recorded member that maps (height, closed, gates as a number, torches: true) is read when no first-class member says otherwise, every other one is listed by name in the part's notes

R18 crossings (T3): a connector.bridge or connector.tunnel needs from and to that resolve to different places; a self-loop answers refused NO_GAP before routing. A bridge whose params name a mechanism or movable (a moving bridge) answers unsupported {block: connector.drawbridge} (S-T3-7). params is read leniently and never makes a T3 part malformed (width, form; material only as a note); every key not read is listed by name in the part's notes
R19 tunnel via (T3, Steward S-T3-6): a tunnel is one straight bore; its via is read leniently: the first leg (from to via[0]) is used and the rest is listed in the part's notes, never malformed
R20 clearance (T3): a bridge's clearance applies only over water; on a dry span it is noted, not read

R21 channels (H): a connector.channel has exactly one path form: where.around (channel.moat) or from/via/to (channel.course); none or both is malformed (SCHEMA) (HY widens it: R24). params is read leniently and never makes an H part malformed: width, depth, fluid, drop and torches/lamps are read when no first-class member says otherwise, lake on a pond is a note only, and every other key (material, existing, mechanism) is listed by name in the part's notes

R22 lava (H): fluid lava (a member on form.pond, or params.fluid elsewhere) is allowed only on form.pond, a lined pit 1..2 deep; anywhere else it answers refused FIRE with evidence.kind lava and the water shape as a wouldFit

R23 ice (H): ice applies only where the biome freezes at the body's surface (the kit's biome table, freezes); elsewhere it is noted, not read. A body in a freezing biome is capped with ice unless ice: false, which is refused WATER {kind: freezes} unless every surface cell is lit to block light 10 or more

R24 courses (HY, R21 widened): a connector.channel has exactly one path form: where.around (channel.moat), from/via/to (channel.course; with a lot {part: <lot>} in via it is a mill race, channel.race) or where.along (channel.ditch); none or two is malformed (SCHEMA). from must stand at least as high as to: an uphill course is refused UNREACHABLE {kind: uphill} with the part with from and to swapped as its wouldFit (never swapped silently). params is read leniently and never makes a course malformed: width, depth, drop, look and flow are read when no first-class member says otherwise; mill, wheel, sluice, lock and material are listed by name in the part's notes, never read

R25 supported aliases (7a, S-7a-3): an alias on a supported entry (aliasOf on a supported connector entry, connector.span_bridge -> connector.bridge): the part is checked against the target's def and answers with the target's block id, noted ("span_bridge is connector.bridge (R25)"); nothing downstream sees the alias

R26 routed 7a connectors (7a): climbs (stair, switchback, ladder), rock stairs, lifts and catwalks are routed connectors (from, to); via is read leniently as R19: the first leg (from to via[0]) is used and the rest noted, never malformed

R27 spiral hosts (7a SA): a connector.stairs_around names its host in around.feature.part, a form part of kind rock_spire, ice_spike, giant_tree or giant_mushroom (an implicit dependency, R3); another part answers refused NO_FEATURE {why: host}

x-defaults.about: Defaults the compiler applies when a member is absent. A contract promise wins over a part's tolerance where both apply (for example C27's within 4 cells for a boundary-following district, once D2 is supported).

tolerance.count.unit: lots of the program left unplaced

tolerance.grade.unit: rise per run over any 8-cell window (T2 maxGrade)

tolerance.sketch.unit: cells between the sketch's centroid and the fitted part's centroid

x-defaults.soft: a soft tolerance may be exceeded up to its ceiling: the part answers adjusted with the deviation and exceeds: true; past the ceiling it is refused
x-defaults.hard: a hard tolerance is never exceeded: the part answers refused with reason TOLERANCE and what would fit
x-defaults.feature.pick: largest, then nearest to the claim's centre, then the smallest min x, then the smallest min z
x-defaults.connector.movers: inferred from the end nodes' lot kinds (T2, S-T2-1); villager edges never use ladders (S-T2-2)

planId.description: Steward's id for the plan, kept across revisions (null or absent: Architect derives none; the check names the plan by its sha).

style.description: The plan's default style bible; a zone's style wins for that zone.

x-catalogue.about: The capability catalogue that P0 ships (catalogueVersion 1). Each entry: a stable block id (never reused or renamed), the API version it arrived in (sinceApi: the API version at which the entry reached its current state and schemaVersion, always a real semver; a new or changed entry carries the branch's placeholder API version and the merge-time renumber restamps it, which tools/catalogue-since-check.mjs enforces), its own schemaVersion (bumped when its members grow, additively), its state (supported | reserved | retired) and, for reserved, the slice it waits for (until). Checks return this catalogue with every answer; a release commits it as a golden so two catalogues diff by id. Reserved entries carry their parameters through $defs/extension until supported.

entries.note: Reserved alias of the districts program form; the answer names program.districts (R4c).
C37 (sinceApi 1.30.0, a placeholder set at merge): additive orientation member (ew | ns | auto) of street layouts.
C37 (sinceApi 1.30.0, a placeholder set at merge): additive orientation member (ew | ns | auto) of street layouts.
N-P0-1: the bundled crater_works program as a named template. A whole-claim program: it compiles only as the plan's sole zone, over the whole claim.
N-P0-1: the bundled rift_city program as a named template. A whole-claim program: it compiles only as the plan's sole zone, over the whole claim.
N-P0-1: the bundled floating_islands program as a named template. A whole-claim program: it compiles only as the plan's sole zone, over the whole claim.
C37 (sinceApi 1.30.0, a placeholder set at merge): additive orientation member (ew | ns | auto) of street layouts.
FL: a closed street round an open hub, lots outside it facing in; central and landmark lots in the hub.
FL: an open street winding out from the hub (up to 3 turns), lots on its outer side; on a hill it climbs to the summit.
FL: blocks of streets (avenues along orientation, cross streets), lots back to back facing the avenues, a central plaza block.
FL: 2 to 4 crooked lanes growing out of a green, lots of mixed setbacks along them.
Lots carried at a level above the ground (canopy huts in trees, cliff ledges): Claude can write them now and they wait as unsupported (S-K1-6).

H: a level ring of water round a feature (channel.moat). HY: courses, races and ditches (channel.course, channel.race, channel.ditch): water that follows the land from a head to a tail, as a chain of level reaches joined by falls and spillways.
An underwater glass passage through water (after H; it builds on H's shell rule); a recorded glass tunnel through water names it instead of connector.tunnel (S-T3-7).
A moving bridge (redstone, a lifting deck): a connector.bridge whose params name a mechanism or movable answers this block (R18, S-T3-7).
A course crosses under a water gate (HY, wall.water_gate): the wall on a lintel over a still reach, an iron grate in the water under it; it counts against gates.max, and a sealed wall refuses it.
Minecart track between stations; carts and rails come later (S-HY-3, S-7a-5).

CW: the face form: a level deck shelf on brackets along a cliff or a steep bank, railed on its open side, where a walk would cut deep or go a long way round; never over water (WATER). Decks between buildings at height wait for 7b.
A deck along a giant tree's branches between canopy lots: needs layout.elevated and F3's branch skeleton (S-7a-4).
A supported alias of connector.bridge (a gap with a floor within 24: the bridge's beam): the part is checked and answered as connector.bridge, noted (R25, S-7a-3).
K1: a wall through from, via[] and to (each leg searched by T2's A* with a wall profile); a lot endpoint is a joined lot.

K1: a wall round a part, build or protected area, or (K1-target) one of the owner's standing regions, around {feature: {region}} (where.around on a wall: the wall's own member, not locator.around; its region not feature.region).
K1: a wall on the edge of a zone or the claim (where.inside).
D2's boundary spine plus an offset (where.along on a wall): the same member, no format change.

HY: where a course crosses a wall's line or ring, the wall stands on a lintel over a still reach and a waterlogged iron grate fills the water under it; still water passes, flowing water and mobs don't. It counts against the wall's gates.max; a sealed wall refuses it (UNREACHABLE wall). No walk gate.
T3: a deck on piers to site-solid ground; H: piers stand in water up to waterDepth, never in flowing water or lava.
T3: one masonry arch between two abutments, no piers (span 4..24).
T3: a level bore through rising ground, portal to portal.
A passage under flat ground whose ends sit in cellars: a tunnel whose every line lacks cover answers this block; it waits for 7b's ports in buildings (K5 forbids writes in lot boxes).

H: a level ring of still water round a feature (where.around; ring default [6, 12]), sunk, lined, closed or capped on the side facing the claim's centre; routes cross it on T3's bridge fallback. HY: may feed a course (overflow) or receive one (a fall over the rim).
A channel along a line (from, via, to) with reaches at several levels or joined to natural water: HY's, built from H's fluid bodies.
HY: a mill race, a course with a lot in via: a wheel fall of at least 3 beside the lot, outside its box (the wheel is the lot design's); the answer names the side and the fall (serves).
HY: a level irrigation ditch 1 wide and 1 deep along the sides of a lot or zone (where.along), outside its box; it hydrates nothing in the lot (working farms are a later block).
A course carried over low ground on piers or arches: what a course needing more than its fill answers (unsupported, with the shape it needs).

B shipped brush strokes as their own regions (Regions.brush, one region per stroke, S-B-1); a stroke's destruction rule lives on its region's record, so a brush part inside a plan's single region waits for a later plan slice.
HY: may feed a course (overflow) or receive one (a fall over the rim).
HY: may feed a course (overflow) or receive one (a fall over the rim).
Inside a plan body only (where.inside a pond, fountain, quay or moat part): written as the body's own cells.
A free-standing crater form. A whole-region crater is already the crater_works template (program.crater_works).
Building under water; a later slice, not yet named.
Structures that move or float; not yet scheduled.
Structures that move or float; not yet scheduled.
measured over parts and bound lots (over: lots: bound lots only); required rules are checked again at realise
Arcology: floors stacked in one volume. RC, or 7b if it needs the interior work.
Upside-down or hanging builds; 7b's other surfaces.
On a wall: wall.around, K1 (the wall's own member). Zones: a ring street round the feature; forms: sites in the band.
PT (C32): a player's build as a plan feature {build: {id | kind, pick?, to?}}; also target {build: id} (inside, adjacent) and near {feature: {build}}. sinceApi is PT's placeholder, set at merge.
PT (C32): {build: id, port?: door | door_<n>}: a road ends on the door's apron (the cells outside it).
polygon: the zone's mask; polyline: the street's line.

anchor.description: A named point: built in (claim_center, claim_n, claim_e, claim_s, claim_w) or supplied by the caller in PlanRequest.anchors (for example stone). Never a coordinate in the plan. Steward passes stone, player, street_w, street_e, district_<id> and stockpile; P0 does not interpret the names.

preset.description: (F3) A species preset by name (the catalogue entry's limits.presets).

ext.description: Opaque, namespaced, bounded (R7). Steward's hook on a part: Architect echoes it and keeps it in the artifact.

partRef.description: The documented hook for Steward's life layer: a part addressed as <partId> inside a plan, or <planId>@<revision>#<partId> from outside one (a stage, a schedule entry, a secret). Ids are stable across revisions: a revision that keeps a part keeps its id.

parent.description: <planId>@<n> of the revision this one changes.

parentArtifact.description: The approved artifact this revision starts from, when there is one.

bibleRef.pending.description: The style bible does not exist yet. A part with a pending style is checked as provisional (like an undesigned building): palette and cost are a range, and approval rebinds once the bible exists (R13).

pending.description: A slug naming the bible-to-be (at most 40 characters).

tolerance.description: Explicit per part; absent members take x-defaults. Only the members that apply to the part's family are read; others are ignored with a note.

size.oneOfMessage: a size is {w, d} in blocks (each an integer or [min, max]) or {preset: S|M|L|XL}
size.description: Presets (blocks, w x d): S 32x32, M 48x48, L 64x64, XL 96x96, each with the size tolerance. Absent: the program's own minimum for its lots.

sketch.description: Optional relative sketch, never world coordinates. q64: 0..64 across the claim's x and z; block: blocks relative to frame anchor (+x east, +z south). v0 uses a point or the centroid of any shape as a soft position target (sketch.point); with outline true the drawing itself is fitted (sketch.outline).

outline.description: true: the outline itself is the requirement (sketch.outline): a polygon is the zone's mask, a polyline the street's line; false or absent: only its centroid and extent guide the fit.

feature.description: A deterministic selector over the survey or the plan. Where several features match, pick chooses (x-defaults feature.pick), with stable tie-breaking.

oneOf.description: (PT, feature.build) a player's build in the claim (Sites.builds): by id, or by kind with pick's ties (x-defaults feature.pick)
(PT) a player's build by id: answers under feature.build (one idea, one block id, R4c)

where.description: One locator (v0 vocabulary). Distances in blocks; the compiler quantises every resolved position to cells.

around.description: A zone laid as a ring street round the feature (a part, water, a build or a protected area), offset into ring (default [6, 32]), lots outside facing it; closed false leaves out the arc nearest the claim's centre. A form: its sites in the band. On a wall it is the wall's own member.

oneOf.description: (D1, endpoint.region) a standing region of the plan's owner beside the claim: the route ends at the cell past one of its street ends (port: that street end's graph node id; absent: the street end nearest the other end) inside the claim's seam (at most 16 columns of overlap), written by this plan's region, which the standing region's own undo never touches
(PT, endpoint.build) a road ending on a build's door apron: port door (its first entrance) or door_<n> (the n-th, from 1)

endpoint.oneOfMessage: an endpoint is {part, port?}, {anchor}, {feature}, {region, port?} or {build, port?}

partBase.description: The loose first check every part passes (R4). Strict per-kind checks follow by dispatch.

extension.description: The bounded envelope (R6) for a reserved, retired or unknown kind: answered unsupported {block}, never malformed while within its bounds. Members named here are checked when present; any other member is carried as-is, so Claude may write a reserved kind in the shape of its draft def.

lot.description: One building of a lot set: the shape of kit/lib/params.mjs validateLots (6c V, X), which the compiler hands to the layout unchanged.

label.description: Free text shown with the lot (the same label as a zone's or connector's); role stays a slug. Never verified.

entry.description: A library entry (id or id@version) already designed for this lot; absent: the building is provisional (a cost range) until Steward binds one.

farmPond.description: (H, S-H-2) A farm lot's small pond: a 3x3, 1-deep sunk water body within 2 of the lot, outside its restore box, removed with the region; only on a claim with no surface water (never added in a freezing biome). Off by default.

irrigate.description: (IRR, S-IRR-1) A working farm's irrigation: one open 1x1 water source in every 9x9 of the farm lot's field (the lot less a 1-column border and its front row), each flush with the field, its four sides farmland, so every field column is within 4 of water. The sources are the region's, inside the lot's box; the lot's design leaves them (the artifact's lots[].irrigation). Set it only for a working or automated farm the card asks for; a homely farm keeps farmPond. false on a lot overrides its zone. Only on a farm lot (villager farm, given or implied by its type); never in a freezing biome. Off by default.

template.description: A named template from the catalogue (program.<name>). v0: flat_village (laid out in the zone's rect), and crater_works, rift_city and floating_islands (N-P0-1; whole-claim programs: only as the plan's sole zone).

params.description: For flat_village, params.orientation. Street orientation (C37, sinceApi 1.30.0): orientation "ew" | "ns" | "auto" (default auto: the layout picks the axis that places more lots, then scores higher, so it depends on the lot sizes). "ew" means the street runs east-west (along x), "ns" north-south (along z). "ew" and "ns" are strict: only that axis is tried, never a fallback, and lots that do not fit are unplaced as ever. If the forced axis places no lot where the other would, the part answers refused NO_ROOM (evidence.orientation names it) and wouldFit holds the same part with the other orientation. The template's own params, checked by the kit's validateParams against the program's declared params; an error is malformed with the param path. A template's lots param is a list of $defs/lot.

layout.description: How the lots are laid out. street (default): one straight street. ring: a closed street round a hub, lots facing in, central lots in the hub. spiral: a street winding out from the hub (up a hill to its top). grid: blocks of streets; only grid reads orientation (the avenues' axis). organic: crooked lanes from a green. Every lot is a rect with a cardinal front facing its street; elevated (K1, reserved until 7b, layout.elevated): lots carried at a level above the ground (canopy huts in trees, cliff ledges); answers unsupported {block: layout.elevated}. Write a free layout here, never as a connector kind (connector.ring_street, connector.grid) or a rule kind (rule.ring_layout).

orientation.description: Street orientation (C37, sinceApi 1.30.0): orientation "ew" | "ns" | "auto" (default auto: the layout picks the axis that places more lots, then scores higher, so it depends on the lot sizes). "ew" means the street runs east-west (along x), "ns" north-south (along z). "ew" and "ns" are strict: only that axis is tried, never a fallback, and lots that do not fit are unplaced as ever. If the forced axis places no lot where the other would, the part answers refused NO_ROOM (evidence.orientation names it) and wouldFit holds the same part with the other orientation.

program.districts.description: Districts (D1, block id program.districts; supported since D1, schemaVersion 1): a settlement of several districts as one zone with program {districts: [...], loopiness?}. Each district is placed on a survey candidate (an area of its size at its level band: the claim's height terciles), laid out as one street of its lots with its shared space, and the districts are joined by routes: a minimum spanning tree by route cost plus the cheapest loops while their added cost stays within loopiness of the tree's (default 0.15). The zone's where and size are not read in v0 (the districts are placed over the claim, around the plan's other zones and forms). A district is unplaced (an adjusted answer, its lots counted against count) when no candidate fits or no route reaches it. Zone kind district (zone.district) is an alias: its program decides, so a district zone with a lots program is a standard zone. A connector names one district as {part: <zone>, port: <district id>} (its street end nearest the other end). District ids share the plan's id namespace with parts and lots.

loopiness.description: Loops added past the spanning tree, as a share of the tree's route cost (1/64 steps). Default 0.15.

district.description: (D1) One district of a districts program: its own street of lots and shared space, on a survey candidate of its size at its level band.

size.description: The district's rect (blocks; a range or a preset resolves to its largest); each side 24..256.

levelBand.description: The claim's height tercile the district sits in (default any).

prefer.description: Candidate tags preferred (each missing one costs; never a refusal).

near.description: Other districts of this program it is placed near (after them, its cost the distance to them).

shared.description: Its shared space (default square when both sides are at least 40, else well).

terraces.description: (S3, S-S3-1) Terraced: the lots are laid down the slope as steps, each lot (with its apron) on its own level, the levels rise apart (consecutive lots share a level where the ground allows); the street becomes routes between the lots' entrances (switchbacks and stairs within the zone's grade tolerance). Rims over 2 high are retained (wall: the bible's structure role, with a rail where the drop is over 3; blend: the relief blends them, a wall where its fill can't reach, noted). Write it on the zone (or district) for terraces inside a zone; form.terrace still stands beside zones. On a flat site: one level, noted. {} takes the defaults.

retain.description: How a rim over 2 high is held (default wall).

stairs.description: Stair flights on the routes between the levels (default true).

program.oneOfMessage: a program is {template, params?}, {lots, layout?} or {districts}

x-dispatch.layout: a lots program whose layout is reserved answers layout.<name> (R4b)

zone.standard.description: A part of the settlement with its own purpose, style and buildings. v0 compiles it to a rect inside the claim laid out by its program.

farmPond.description: (H, S-H-2) Every farm lot of the zone gets a farm pond (as a lot's farmPond). Off by default.

irrigate.description: (IRR, S-IRR-1) Every farm lot of the zone is irrigated (as a lot's irrigate; its own false wins). Off by default.

terraces.description: (S3) The zone's lots on terraced levels down the slope (a lots program; placed as one district on its locator's candidates).

purpose.description: A short tag (market, farming, mining, temple). Recorded and echoed; not interpreted in v0.

zone.outpost.description: (D2, zone.outpost) An outpost: a district not touching the town, placed on a survey candidate at least gap (default 24) from every zone and form before it and joined by a road to the nearest other zone's street end; the road's corridor is reported as settlement land and undone with the outpost (one region). Otherwise as zone.standard: a part of the settlement with its own purpose, style and buildings. v0 compiles it to a rect inside the claim laid out by its program.

purpose.description: A short tag (market, farming, mining, temple). Recorded and echoed; not interpreted in v0.

gap.description: Columns kept from the zones and forms resolved before it (default 24).

connector.routed.description: street, road or path, routed by T2 (A* with heading, the grade limit, switchbacks, stairs; ladders only on player-only edges). street: a road with lamps along it (lamps street by default); road: a road between places; path: a narrow walk (stairs allowed).

via.description: Waypoints in order; each leg is one T2 edge.

avoid.description: Features the route keeps out of (as T2 keep-out).

width.description: Road width in cells, for street, road and path alike: 1-5, the range 4e's ground roads (and so T2's routes) support. Defaults in x-defaults (street 3, road 3, path 1).

movers.description: The per-edge override S-T2-1 left room for; absent: inferred.

wallWhere.description: (K1) A wall's own path form (its where): around a part, build or protected area (wall.around; ring is the offset range, default [4, 12]; closed: false leaves out the side nearest the claim's centre), on the edge of a zone or the claim (wall.edge), or along a boundary (wall.along, reserved until K2). Not locator.around: on a wall it is the wall's own member.

inside.oneOfMessage: a wall's inside is {claim: true} or {part}

connector.wall.description: (K1) A wall on a line (wall.line: from, via[], to), around a feature (wall.around) or on the edge of a zone or the claim (wall.edge), R15. Height 3..16 (default 6: 5 body plus the crenel course), thickness 1..3 (default 2, on the outside of a ring), crenels (default on), plain corners (default) or 3x3 corner stubs, styled by the bible's connectors roles. Every crossing of a street, road or path gets a gate (auto), except on a sealed wall (gates 0, or closed with no gate part). params is read leniently (R17).

gates.oneOfMessage: gates is an integer 0..16 (the least on a closed wall) or {min?, max?}

waterDepth.description: (H) The deepest natural water the wall may stand in (a harbour wall; default 6). Only a wall that fails on water is searched again with wet sections (the wet fallback).

params.description: Read leniently, never malformed (R17): height, closed, gates (a number) and torches: true are read when no first-class member says otherwise; every other key is listed in the answer's notes.

connector.gate.description: (K1) An opening in a wall where a street, road or path crosses it: placed at an endpoint (at, before routing), named by the connector whose route opens it (crossing, after routing), or styling the plan's one wall's gate. A gate written from/to is read as at: from (R16). width 1..5 (default the crossing walk's), height 2..6 (default 3), door none (default), door (a wooden double door, R17) or fence_gate (player-only), frame plain or arch (default arch).

params.description: Read leniently, never malformed (R17); every key is listed in the answer's notes.

connector.rope_bridge.description: (K1) A rope bridge (SETTLEMENTS §8.2): a route between from and to that uses exactly one rope span (8..40 deck cells, an integer half-block sag profile, rails, posts anchored 2 deep in site-solid at both ends), walking at most approach cells (default 16) at each end. width 1..3 (default 1 on a player-only edge, 2 on a villager edge: a villager bridge is 2 wide on a slab deck).

params.description: Read leniently, never malformed (R17); every key is listed in the answer's notes.

connector.auto.description: (K1) A route that may use any move the catalogue lists in limits.moves (walk, stairs, ladders on player-only edges, rope bridges; T3: bridges and tunnels, a tunnel only inside a frozen volume the plan already holds), each costed as T2 and the special moves (S-K1-5: the move set grows as slices ship). span stays the rope move's (8..40); bridges take their own limits.

params.description: Read leniently, never malformed (R17); every key is listed in the answer's notes.

connector.bridge.description: (T3) A bridge: a route from from to to over exactly one built span (a gap or water), walking at most approach (default 16) at each end. form: beam (deck on piers, bridge.beam), arch (span 4..24, bridge.arch), auto (default: arch where it fits). width default 2 villager, 1 player-only. clearance: clear cells over water (default 2; R20). No write in water or ice, except H's wet fallback: a crossing that fails only on water is searched again with piers in natural water sources up to waterDepth (default 8; never flowing water, lava or a bubble column); past that it refuses WATER {kind: deep | flowing | lava}. R18.

waterDepth.description: (H) The deepest natural water a pier may stand in (default 8). Only a crossing that fails on water is searched again with wet piers (the wet fallback).

params.description: Read leniently (R18): width, form; every other key noted.

connector.tunnel.description: (T3) A tunnel (tunnel.through): one straight level bore through rising ground, portal to portal, lined where soil, sand or ice shows, lit, 2 cells from any fluid, walking at most approach (default 16) at each end. width default 3 villager, 2 player-only; height 2..5 clear (default 3); lining exposed (default) or all; portal arch (default) or plain. Flat ground between the ends answers unsupported {tunnel.under, until 7b}. R18, R19.

params.description: Read leniently (R18): width; every other key noted.

connector.stair.description: (7a CL) A climb in stair flights (T2's stair profile), railed beside drops. Ends rising under 2: refused NO_CLIMB (a path wouldFit); walked within the grade: adjusted (deviation climb). R26.

connector.switchback.description: (7a CL) A climb on hairpins, no flights (T2's switchback profile), retaining walls in the bible's role (none: T2's). NO_CLIMB as a stair. R26.

connector.ladder.description: (7a CL) A climb up a face to 48 (T2's ladder profile), player-only (movers naming villager: refused MOVER), a rest landing every rest rungs, a fence gate on top; every rung against a sturdy face (else ANCHOR). NO_CLIMB as a stair. R26.

connector.rock_stair.description: (7a RK) A stair flight carved into rising ground (route row 11); needs a frozen volume. R26.

connector.lift.description: (7a LF) A bubble column against a face (route row 9), player-only; down: a second column. R26.

connector.catwalk.description: (7a CW) A bracketed deck along a face (route row 10). R26.

connector.stairs_around.description: (7a SA) A spiral stair round a form part (R27: a rock_spire, ice_spike, giant_tree or giant_mushroom) up to a lookout.

connector.channel.description: (H, HY) A channel of water. One path form (R21, R24): where.around (channel.moat: a level ring round a feature at ring offsets, default [6, 12], width 1..7 (default 5) and depth 1..4 (default 3), surface 1 under the ground, sunk and lined; closed: false leaves the side facing the claim's centre capped); from/via/to (channel.course: water that follows the land from a head down to a tail, as level reaches joined by falls and spillways, width 1..5 and depth 1..3, look natural (a stream, default) or built (a canal), flow pools (default), level or riffles, drop the highest single fall 1..8 (default 6); with a lot ({part: <lot>}) in via it is a mill race, channel.race); or where.along (channel.ditch: a level irrigation ditch 1 x 1 along the sides of a lot or zone, outside its box). from must stand at least as high as to (else refused UNREACHABLE uphill, with the swapped wouldFit). Streets, roads and paths cross a moat or a course on T3's bridge fallback (clearance 1 over plan water), landing at a wall's gate. params read leniently (R21, R24): width, depth, drop, look, flow; mill, wheel, sluice, lock and material noted, never read.

along.description: (HY, channel.ditch) the lot or zone a ditch runs beside (feature {part}); sides: which sides of its box (default the two long sides)

look.description: (HY) a course's look: natural (a stream: a clay and mud bed, mossy banks) or built (a canal in the structure role with a trim coping)

flow.description: (HY) a course's profile: pools (default: level reaches joined by falls and spillways), level (one reach: a canal), riffles (opt-in: visible current over a stepped bed, capped)

drop.description: (HY) the highest single fall of a course (default 6)

form.relief.description: T1's relief pass: blends the land into the pads and corridors of the parts named (target pads stay flat).

form.terrace.description: Flat steps cut into a slope (6a terrace), their edges blended by T1's relief (edge blend) or 1:1 batters (edge slope).

form.spike.description: F1's generators: ice_spike (packed and blue ice, snow caps; never ice or snow layers) and rock_spire.

keepNatural.description: ice_spike: keep the claim's natural spikes (F1 r.keepNatural).

form.giant_tree.description: F3: a giant tree (log trunk and branches, persistent leaves; crimson and warped: stems, wart caps, shroomlight), on open land: never within 8 of a natural tree, never over a lot, street, path, wall or body.

form.giant_mushroom.description: F3: a giant mushroom (stem, a flat brown or domed red cap), placed as giant_tree.

form.coral.description: F3: live coral, fans and sea pickles on the bed of a plan body; where.inside names the pond, fountain, quay or moat.

form.roots.description: F3: roots down a steep face or from a cave ceiling (rooted dirt, hanging roots; mangrove: mangrove roots); a ceiling needs a frozen volume.

form.stalactites.description: F3: dripstone cones from a cave ceiling and the floor under it, columns where they meet; needs a frozen volume.

form.pond.description: (H) A pond: still water (or a lined lava pit, fluid lava, 1..2 deep) sunk 1 under the lowest ground of its rim, depth (default 2) at the centre stepping up 1 per ring, in a 1-thick shell; edge natural (default: a bed of the bible's fluids.bed, plants in the shallows) or built (structure with a 1-high coping). Capped with ice where the biome freezes (ice: false refuses WATER {kind: freezes} unless lit). params read leniently (R21): depth, fluid, lake (a note); every other key noted.

ice.description: Default: capped where the biome freezes (R23); false keeps the surface open, refused WATER {kind: freezes} there unless lit.

form.fountain.description: (H) A fountain: a built basin (basin cells square, odd, 3..9; 1 deep, raised 1 over the ground, a trim coping thick enough to pass the single breach) with a 1x1 spout pillar spout cells (1..4) over the rim, a source on top whose four sides fall into the basin. Water only (R22). params read leniently (R21).

basin.description: The basin's side in cells, odd (default 5).

spout.description: The spout's height over the rim (default 2).

form.waterfall.description: (H) A waterfall: a raised header pool (sources at the lip), a lip run and a falling column (declared spill) of width (1..5, default 3) one cell out from the face, dropping drop (3..24) into a basin: a pond body or a join into natural water at least 2 deep (basin auto, pond or join). lip existing uses a natural drop within where; sculpt raises a rock outcrop (at most 12 high) in stage ground; auto (default) is existing where one passes, else sculpt. A flowing waterfall already in the world is never adopted; the hollow behind it is 7b's (form.hidden_room). params read leniently (R21): existing is read as lip auto (noted).

form.quay.description: (H) A quay: a level deck from the shore out over natural water (reach 1..6 cells, default 3; length 4..48), 1 over the surface, solid to a footing 2 into the bed, with mooring posts every 4, lamps, and a step down to the water every 16 (the exits). Needs natural water within its locator (NO_FEATURE otherwise). params read leniently (R21).

rule.common.description: Members every rule has. Rules are verified on the fitted output with evidence (the rule-check slice, RC); in plan/0 every rule kind but palette (VOC-c: measured) is reserved and answers unsupported. The drafts below are guidance for the plan writer; RC makes them strict, widening only additively.

scope.description: Parts the rule binds; absent: the whole plan.

rule.palette.description: (VOC-c) A family's share of the measured cells (written, not air, fluid or common natural) of the parts in scope and their zones' bound lots, less terrain and support (exempt, default both; also ways, forms). over: lots measures the bound lots alone. family: a vocab/1 family or group (wood). share [min, max], default [1, 1]: only X is [1, 1], no X is [0, 0] (re-planned, X swapped along its material chain). Read from params too. A required rule over lots without an entry is checked at realiseApproved (PALETTE).

scope.description: Parts the rule binds; absent: the whole plan.

params.description: Read leniently, never malformed: family, share, exempt and over when the top level leaves them out; other keys (gradient, colours, material) noted, not read.

rule.shape.description: At the outline or footprint level, above voxel faces: no_right_angles, symmetric, round.

rule.variety.description: Measured on the built output (0b's lever metric), for example no two alike.

dependency.description: part stands after every part in after (stage order), and answers blocked when any of them is not fits or adjusted. Implicit dependencies (R3) need no entry.

until.description: reserved: the slice expected to bring it.

aliasOf.description: An alias: the answer names this block id instead of the entry's own, so one idea has one block id. On a reserved entry (R4c) the part answers unsupported under the target; on a supported entry (R25, 7a) the part is checked against the target's def and answered as the target, noted.

path.description: SCHEMA: the JSON path of the first error.

partAnswer.description: One part's answer from Regions.checkPlan (docs/CONTRACT.md P0 §3). blocked: also on a piece (lot, district) its part could not place; blockedBy names the part, the evidence the piece.

geometry.description: Resolved, in world cells: rect or polygon, y, lots (LotSpec shape), path polylines, form bounds.

cost.description: For a provisional part (a building without a library entry, or a pending style) the range form is used and the artifact also records the part's fit box (R13). {cells, removed, added, tiles, chunksToGenerate, bom?} exact, or {range: {cells: [min, max], bom?}} when provisional.

items.description: A concrete alternative as a plan fragment (for example a smaller size, another where) with its own geometry and cost.

ext.description: The part's own ext, echoed unchanged (Steward's hook).

notes.description: What the check did with the part that is not a deviation or a reason (for example a member v0 reads but does not act on). Never a verified requirement.

measured.description: (VOC-c) A palette rule's measure: {cells, family, share, parts: {id: [family, cells]}, lots: {id: [family, cells]}, pendingLots} (at most 16 parts and 16 lots, the worst first).
